computational_background: functions, loops, arrays, and plotting in Python
able to run short scripts and inspect numerical output
learning_goals: recognise optimality, smoothness, convexity, and strong convexity conditions
compare momentum, stochastic, and second-order methods
preferred_contexts: mechanical parameter fitting and repeated simulation evaluation
target_depth: Conceptual and mathematical understanding sufficient to implement core algorithms and read convergence statements; no formal convex-optimisation background assumed.
proof_depth: Explain the role of assumptions and bounds, with short derivational bridges rather than full proofs.
assumptions_requiring_review: A potential-energy analogy is not an identity for every engineering model.
A stationary point is not automatically a minimum.
Convergence claims apply only under their stated assumptions.
Stochastic and adaptive methods require care about noise, steps, and stability.
